the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_zai-glm-5-turbo_01.html`.
I'll generate the complete CHIP-8 emulator as a single self-contained HTML file.

- Timers decrement at 60 Hz (in the requestAnimationFrame tick, once per frame).
- Full instruction set (35 ops): 00E0 CLS, 00EE RET, 1nnn JP, 2nnn CALL, 3xkk SE Vx,kk, 4xkk SNE, 5xy0 SE Vx,Vy, 6xkk LD, 7xkk ADD, 8xy0/1/2/3/4/5/6/7/E (ALU: OR, AND, XOR, ADD with VF carry, SUB with VF borrow=Vx<Vy, SHR VF=lsb, SUBN VF=Vy<Vx, SHL VF=msb — shifts use Vx value), 9xy0 SNE Vx,Vy, Annn LD I, Bnnn JP V0+nnn, Cxkk RND (Math.random), Dxyn DRW (XOR draw, wrap coordinates, VF=collision), Ex9E/ExA1 key tests (ExA1 skip if not pressed; if waitingKey mode pending, block PC until key pressed), Fx07/Fx15 (delay timer), Fx18 (sound timer), Fx1E (I+=Vx), Fx0A (wait key), Fx29 (I=font char), Fx33 BCD (hundreds/tens/ones at I), Fx55/Fx65 (save/load V0..Vx to memory starting at I, then increment I by x+1).

- Set I to sprite addr (load sprite bytes at a fixed address in ROM via self-copy, or simpler: place sprite data in the ROM and set I using Annn where nnn = 0x200+offset — sprite data can just live in code space after the code).
Program sketch:
  0x200: A2 XX      ; I = sprite address
  6E 0A 6F 05       ; VE=10 (x), VF=5 (y)  -> actually use VE as x, VF as y? VF is flag reg, better use V0=x V1=y
  Loop:
  00E0              ; clear
  D0 15             ; draw sprite (8 wide, 5 tall) at V0,V1
  F0 0A             ; wait for key press (blocks) — simpler & reliably reactive
  ... then compare pressed key: Fx29 not needed; after F00A the key value is in V0? No — Fx0A waits and stores key in Vx. So use F10A wait key into V1? But V1 is y. Use: F20A (wait key into V2), then check V2==6 -> x+=2 (72xx), V2==4 -> x-=2, V2==8 -> y-=2, V2==2 -> y+=2, then jump back to loop.
  Comparisons: 326 → skip if V2==6; use sequence:
    426 JP skip... easier: 
    3206 -> skip next if V2==6 ; then 70 02 (V0+=2) jump loop
  Sprite bytes: e.g. 0x3C,0x7E,0xFF,0xFF,0x7E (a diamond) 5 rows.
Write the demo as a hex byte array in JS with a comment table explaining each instruction. Verify addresses: code starts 0x200. Place sprite right after code; compute its absolute address and encode into the Annn instruction. Make sure BNNN/jumps use correct absolute addresses — assemble carefully so the demo actually runs.

KEYBOARD: map 1234/QWER/ASDF/ZXCV to CHIP-8 keys 1,2,3,C / 4,5,6,D / 7,8,9,E / A,0,B,F. keydown/keyup set keys[n]. Also show clickable on-screen 4x4 keypad buttons (mousedown/mouseup + touchstart/touchend) that highlight when pressed.

DEBUGGER PANEL: update every frame (and after step): V0-VF hex, I, PC, SP/stack contents list, delay/sound timers, current opcode hex + decoded disassembly string (e.g. "D015  DRW V0, V1, 5"). Disassembler function covering all opcodes.

MAIN LOOP: requestAnimationFrame; per frame: decrement timers, run N instructions (N = speed slider) if running; render display to canvas each frame; update debug panel. Step button: execute exactly 1 instruction + render/update. Reset: reload current ROM bytes (demo or loaded), clear state.

Sound: optional tiny WebAudio beep when st>0 (keep it simple, guard against AudioContext errors).

Everything inline, no external anything. Write clean, commented code."}
